papers.title: Stopping and Routing LLM Judge Panels

summary.tldr: A new role-conditioned allocation framework optimizes LLM judge panels by classifying candidate judges into roles to derive cost-effective stopping and routing policies from a small audit set.
key_points: Formulates panel design as a role-conditioned allocation problem using a small labeled audit set, declared data slices, and execution costs.
Categorizes candidate judges into target-relative roles: copies (no conditional info), complements (global panel improvements), and specialists (slice-specific utility).
Generates an actionable policy that drops copies, adds complements globally, routes specialists to specific slices, and stops execution when validation gain drops below a cost threshold.
Evaluated across reasoning, code, safety, preference, reward-model, summarization, and math domain audits.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces ad-hoc or full-ensemble judge calls with an auditable, cost-efficient call plan that optimizes inference spending while maintaining evaluation accuracy.

papers.title: Projector Is All You Train

summary.tldr: Training only the projector in multimodal LLMs delivers strong performance on 3D tasks without needing to fine-tune the language backbone.
key_points: Projector-only training achieves performance competitive with joint training on 3D classification, 3D captioning, and spatial reasoning benchmarks.
Freezing the language backbone prevents catastrophic forgetting and drift in pre-existing language capabilities caused by joint training.
Projector-only training achieves approximately twice the training sample throughput compared to joint backbone-projector training.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces MLLM training compute costs and speeds up throughput while fully preserving original language model capabilities.

papers.title: Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a statistical model that smoothes low-sample rollout data to efficiently estimate uncertainty dynamics in LLM text generation at a fraction of the computational cost.
key_points: Resampling text sequences at every token or sentence to measure uncertainty dynamics is computationally expensive.
Uncertainty dynamics converge to stable patterns when resampling many reasoning chains, indicating noise is primarily a sampling artifact rather than LLM sensitivity to specific tokens or steps.
The introduced statistical model smoothes noisy, low-sample rollout data to accurately approximate high-sample data, reducing overall sampling requirements.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables researchers to analyze LLM reasoning chains and uncertainty dynamics far more efficiently without incurring the massive computational overhead of extensive sequence resampling.

papers.title: When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models

summary.tldr: UniLang expands pretrained LLM vocabulary and embedding spaces to autoregressively generate machine-native discrete symbols alongside natural-language tokens within a unified framework.
key_points: Extends LLM vocabulary and embedding spaces with grounded machine-native representations.
Eliminates the need to verbalize structured representations into natural language or rely on task-specific architectures.
Jointly models textual and symbolic tokens under a single autoregressive generative objective.
Demonstrates performance improvements over strong baselines on sequential recommendation and legal precedent prediction tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLMs to serve as a unified generative backbone for structured prediction and machine-native data without losing domain-specific structural information.

papers.title: Break It Down, Pass It On: Cross-Task Skill Transfer in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: A controlled study reveals that subtask-level and text-formatted skills transfer better in LLM agents than task-level and code-based skills, introducing a non-execution-based skill utility score to predict transfer success.
key_points: Subtask-level skill induction increases agent performance over no-memory baselines, whereas task-level skills generally degrade performance.
Text-formatted skills exhibit better cross-task transfer performance compared to code-formatted skills.
Skill transfer success depends on the combined effect of specificity (match to real tasks) and abstractness (relevance distribution across tasks).
The authors introduce a skill utility score calculated using only skill and task descriptions, enabling memory diagnosis prior to task execution.
summary.why_it_matters: System designers can improve LLM agent memory reliability and diagnose skill quality before execution without running costly, multi-step task evaluations.

papers.title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference

summary.tldr: Daedalus-150M is a 4-bit CPU-optimized language model that replaces full attention with 2-timestep short convolutions in 12 of its 18 blocks, achieving faster decode speeds and higher benchmark scores.
key_points: Architecture retains full attention in only 6 of 18 blocks, using short convolutions with a constant 2-timestep memory width for the remaining 12 blocks to eliminate KV cache growth.
Trained from scratch on 59.9B tokens, scoring 47.31 on a five-task benchmark and achieving a validation bits-per-byte of 0.8685.
Delivers 1.76x faster decoding at 2048 tokens context and a 6.3% smaller 4-bit file size compared to an equivalent all-attention baseline trained on identical data.
Outperforms GPT-2 124M, Pythia-160M, OPT-125M, GPT-neo-125M, and MobileLLM-125M on benchmarks despite using significantly less training data.
Negative findings include an unmitigated 4-bit quality penalty, an oversized vocabulary, and roughly half of the convolution channels becoming inert without a way to remove them.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that replacing attention with fixed-memory convolutions in most transformer layers significantly improves CPU inference speed and context scaling without sacrificing task quality.

papers.title: Optimal Skill Selection for LLM Agents with Provable Bicriteria Guarantees

summary.tldr: Best Prefix Selection (BPS) optimizes LLM agent skill retrieval under token budgets, achieving a provable bicriteria (1-1/e, 1) approximation guarantee.
key_points: Skill selection is modeled as an optimization problem: maximizing a monotone submodular benefit minus context penalty under a hard token budget.
Best Prefix Selection (BPS) is a polynomial-time algorithm providing a bicriteria (1-1/e, 1) approximation guarantee with an optimal benefit coefficient.
On a contamination-controlled BigCodeBench variant, BPS achieved a 0.73 task success rate compared to 0.20-0.52 for baseline skill routers and retrievers.
BPS reduced token consumption by 28% relative to the strongest released skill router baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates context window waste and performance degradation caused by independent semantic scoring and greedy skill packing in LLM agents.

papers.title: Interrupting the Loop: Periodic Subject Changes Raise Judged Surprise and Connection in Base Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers isolated a specific mechanism in base LLMs where injecting periodic subject interruptions combined with habituation significantly increases judged surprise and connection, though it fails to produce cohesive long-form documents.
key_points: Injecting a new subject every 150-300 tokens alongside habituation increases judged surprise by 1.2-1.4 points and connection by 0.8 points over habituation alone.

Evaluating windowed text revealed vulnerabilities: LLM judges misattribute experimenter-injected sentences as model output and rate looped model replays from beyond the context horizon as novel surprise and connection.
Complex additions like salience monitors, in-loop judges, kept context vs. reset context, and connective prompts added no detectable value over simple interruptions.
On an online bin-packing task, subject interruption increased valid, distinct candidate heuristics three- to fourfold without improving the peak heuristic quality.
summary.why_it_matters: Periodic subject interruption provides a simple method to boost local creative diversity in base LLMs, while highlighting critical flaws in window-based LLM evaluation protocols for long text generation.

papers.title: EXIMO: VLM Guided Exploration of VLA Policies

summary.tldr: EXIMO is a three-stage finetuning framework that uses a Vision-Language Model planner to guide Vision-Language-Action policies through exploration, imitation, and residual off-policy reinforcement learning.
key_points: Operates in three sequential stages: explore, imitate, and optimize.
The explore stage uses a VLM as a high-level planner to decompose long-horizon tasks into sub-goals for the VLA model to generate an orchestrated dataset.
The imitate stage finetunes the VLA policy directly on the collected orchestrated dataset.
The optimize stage applies residual off-policy reinforcement learning to refine the finetuned VLA policy.
Addresses sample inefficiency and high teleoperation data collection costs for robotic task adaptation.
summary.why_it_matters: EXIMO enables sample-efficient online adaptation of large VLA robot policies for new, long-horizon manipulation tasks without requiring extensive human teleoperation.

papers.title: Write Once, Run Everywhere: The Axon DSL for Shape-Safe and Framework-Agnostic LLM Architectures

summary.tldr: Axon is a strongly typed, Haskell-like domain-specific language that allows developers to write LLM architectures once and compile them directly to PyTorch, Triton, JAX, MLX, and vLLM.
key_points: Compiles concise, auditable model specifications into standalone implementations for PyTorch, PyTorch+Triton, JAX, MLX, and vLLM.
Eliminates framework lock-in by decoupling model architecture design from underlying training and inference runtime engines.
Demonstrates median inference speedups over Hugging Face Transformers of 7% on PyTorch, 12% on PyTorch with Triton, 91% on JAX, and 107% on MLX across models from 135M to 32B parameters.
Achieves a 58% median speedup over Transformers when deployed as native vLLM architectures using PagedAttention and KV-cache.
summary.why_it_matters: Axon reduces the engineering burden of translating models across frameworks while delivering significant inference performance gains over standard reference implementations.

papers.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning

summary.tldr: EnvHarness introduces a programmable layer of plug-in components that dynamically reshapes static environments around black-box agents without altering underlying logic or original verifiers.
key_points: EnvHarness wraps static environments using standard interfaces, preserving original verifiers across diverse domains without rewriting underlying code.
EnvRigger automates harness creation by observing black-box execution trajectories, diagnosing flaws, synthesizing targeted components, and validating via fresh rollouts.
The framework improved task performance by up to 9.0 points on held-out instances while reducing execution steps by 9.8% across five benchmarks in four domains.
Provides an improved optimization signal for reinforcement learning, facilitating continuous co-evolution between the policy and its environment.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need to manually engineer complex, domain-specific environment generation pipelines for LLM agent reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Listening Forward: Next Patch Embedding Prediction Enables Scalable Audio Learners

summary.tldr: NAPE introduces a minimalist self-supervised audio framework that uses a causal Transformer to predict the next log-mel spectrogram patch embedding using only causal masking and stop-gradients.
key_points: Predicts continuous next-patch embeddings sequentially from previous log-mel spectrogram context.
Eliminates student-teacher setups, acoustic tokenizers, reconstruction decoders, and auxiliary losses.
Demonstrates consistent scaling across encoder sizes and strong performance in both fine-tuning and linear-probing evaluations across six audio and speech benchmarks.
Generates structured attention patterns without requiring explicit supervision.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that simple autoregressive embedding prediction can match or exceed complex audio SSL pipelines, offering a unified pre-training strategy across modalities.

papers.title: Which Eviction Policy Should an LLM Cache Use? A Systematic Study Across Workloads, Capacities, and Encoders

summary.tldr: A systematic evaluation using the CLEVER protocol shows that LFU is the strongest simple eviction default for LLM semantic caches, as complex geometry-aware policies offer virtually no improvement over it.
key_points: No evaluated policy (FIFO, LRU, LFU, ARC, GDSF, streaming SISO, or semantic-redundancy) beats LFU by more than 0.041 percentage points across 18 experimental configurations.
Eviction policy choice still impacts performance: FIFO and streaming SISO underperform LFU by up to 8.67 and 8.55 percentage points, respectively, under tight cache constraints.
Geometry-aware eviction rules fail to add value due to conditional packing: under exact lookup and insert-on-miss, new entries never have resident neighbors within the hit radius.
At MiniLM's median nearest-neighbor threshold, only 2.1-3.9% of LMSYS and QQP hits are answer-substitutable, causing raw hit rates of 51-60% to drop to quality-adjusted rates of 1.1-2.2%.
Similarity thresholds do not transfer reliably between different embedding models.
summary.why_it_matters: System designers should default to LFU and focus on verifying answer validity and embedding-specific thresholds rather than implementing complex semantic eviction algorithms.

papers.title: Ask Self, Ask Others: Relation Is All You Need

summary.tldr: Relation is a token-mixing primitive that explicitly separates pairwise evidence into Self and Exchange relations before deriving information flow, outperforming Multi-Head Attention in validation loss.
key_points: Replaces standard attention by organizing pairwise evidence into explicit Self and Exchange relations prior to computing information flow.
Introduces variants including Full Relation, FlashRelation, Linear Relation, Hybrid Relation, and a KV-style Relation Cache.
Full Relation achieves lower final validation NLL compared to Multi-Head Attention across 10M, 30M, and 100M parameter decoder-only models.
FlashRelation speeds up execution by 3.60-4.41x over the materialized Full Relation baseline and reaches 76.4-84.9% of PyTorch FlashAttention throughput.
Hybrid Relation retains strong language-modeling quality while using 75% Linear Relation layers.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that a relation-first approach to token mixing can improve language model validation loss while offering hardware-efficient execution variants comparable to FlashAttention.

papers.title: Feature Evolution and Migration during Vision Transformer Training

summary.tldr: A novel framework uses Sparse Autoencoders on CLS-token representations across training time and network depth to track feature evolution and feature migration in Vision Transformers.
key_points: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) extract candidate sparse features from ViT CLS-token representations to analyze epoch-layer activation profiles.
Feature migration—the shift in the layer where a feature is most detectable during training—is concentrated in early training epochs.
Features migrate more frequently toward earlier layers than toward deeper layers, declining as feature organization stabilizes.
Deeper ViT layers stabilize earlier and more strongly than shallow layers during training.
summary.why_it_matters: This methodology provides a fine-grained feature-level tool to track, visualize, and understand internal model dynamics and layer-wise stabilization during ViT training.

papers.title: Reward-Guided Autoregressive Graph Generation for Efficient Multi-Agent Communication Topology Design

summary.tldr: RGA-Designer introduces an RLHF-inspired reward-guided autoregressive graph generation approach to design sparse multi-agent communication topologies that maintain reasoning accuracy while reducing token usage.
key_points: RGA-Designer trains a dedicated reward model that simultaneously evaluates task correctness and structural compactness.
The pretrained autoregressive graph generator is fine-tuned using feedback directly from the trained reward model.
The method achieves an average token reduction of 20.5% compared to ARG-Designer while maintaining comparable task accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces LLM multi-agent operational costs by optimizing communication topology compactness without sacrificing task performance.

papers.title: Orthogonal JEPA: Factorized Predictive States for Latent World Models

summary.tldr: Orthogonal JEPA introduces orthogonal predictive factorization to latent world models, decomposing target states into distinct components predicted by dedicated branches from a shared context to prevent monolithic state redundancy.
key_points: Decomposes latent target states into multiple components using learned basis matrices and dedicated prediction branches derived from a shared context representation.
Uses an orthogonality objective to discourage redundant component directions and a factor-activity regularization to preserve target variation.
Applies predictive regression to maintain factor magnitudes for state synthesis alongside online variance regularization to prevent encoder collapse.
Synthesizes predicted components into complete latent states suitable for readouts, decoders, planners, and autoregressive rollouts across temporal and spatial tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: By preventing dominant signals from overcrowding the latent space, Orthogonal JEPA improves predictive representation quality, long-horizon stability, and planning across complex, multi-scale dynamical systems.

papers.title: Scale-Aware Pretraining of Time Series Foundation Models via Multi-Patch Token Alignment and Hybrid Masking

summary.tldr: SATS introduces scale-aware pretraining for time series foundation models using multi-patch token alignment and a novel hybrid masking strategy.
key_points: SATS uses a scale-aware token alignment mechanism with a contrastive-inspired regularizer to align multi-scale patch size representations while maintaining modeling capacity.
A hybrid masking strategy combining random and contiguous masking is implemented to capture multi-scale temporal structures across heterogeneous datasets.
Outperforms competitive baselines on LSTF benchmarks with a 9.2% reduction in MSE and an 8.3% improvement in GIFT-Eval MASE.
Achieves a 65.6% increase in model efficiency over advanced time series pretraining baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves representation fragmentation caused by varying temporal sampling frequencies, delivering state-of-the-art accuracy with significantly lower computational overhead.

papers.title: PolicyGuide: From Guarding One Action to Guiding the Whole Workflow for Policy-Compliant LLM Agents

summary.tldr: PolicyGuide compiles domain policies into workflow graphs and uses proactive verifiers at user-turn boundaries to provide step-specific remediation for policy-compliant LLM agents.
key_points: Compiles domain policies into workflow graphs and tracks persisted graph state across user turns.
Proactive verifier reconciles open requests and directs agents along policy-compliant paths to prevent forbidden actions and procedural omissions.
Increases mean Pass^4 from 0.42 to 0.62 across τ^2-bench domains using GPT-5.4, with telecom performance rising from 0.19 to 0.61.
Demonstrates transferability across Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 2.5 Pro agents while achieving lower adversarial attack-success rates.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts LLM safety from reactive, single-action checks to proactive, multi-step procedural guidance across complex customer-service workflows.

papers.title: MileGPO: Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization of Long-Horizon LLM Agents

summary.tldr: MileGPO improves long-horizon LLM agent RL by inferring process-level milestones and traps from grouped on-policy rollouts using Reliability-Calibrated Shaping and Progress-Contrastive Calibration without extra environment interactions or auxiliary models.
key_points: Milestone Discovery locates candidate success milestones on successful rollouts and recurring traps on failed rollouts.
Reliability-Calibrated Shaping (RCS) scales candidates using outcome-based confidence weights to emphasize reliable trajectories.
Progress-Contrastive Calibration (PCC) validates whether candidates represent local progress and if incoming transitions outperform same-state alternatives.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on ALFWorld and WebShop benchmarks with a minimal in-distribution to out-of-distribution gap on ALFWorld.
summary.why_it_matters: MileGPO solves fine-grained credit assignment in sparse-reward environments without requiring auxiliary models or extra environment sampling.

papers.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: ConceptGuard is a new benchmark for LLM unlearning that uses dual-use concepts to evaluate intent-sensitive contextual separation between harmful and benign uses of the same concept.
key_points: Addresses the limitation of current unlearning benchmarks that rely on disjoint, independent forget and retain sets evaluated via direct factual recall.
Introduces dual-use concepts, which pair harmful target usages with benign complementary usages of the same concept.
Evaluates methods based on their contextual separation performance, ROUGE scores, and consistency in concept-level control.
Demonstrates that existing LLM unlearning techniques exhibit strong forgetting-utility trade-offs and fail to maintain fine-grained contextual sensitivity.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a realistic benchmark for verifying that LLMs can forget malicious applications of sensitive knowledge without destroying the model's useful, benign capabilities.

papers.title: FormalTCS: Benchmarking End-to-End Frontier Formal Theoretical Computer Science Research of Large Language Models

summary.tldr: FormalTCS is a benchmark of 175 Lean-formalized instances from recent STOC, FOCS, SODA, and COLT papers designed to evaluate LLMs on end-to-end theoretical computer science research.
key_points: Evaluates models using 175 expert-verified Lean formalizations and proofs based on 2025-2026 conference papers.

Identifies autoformalization as the primary bottleneck, with the best model scoring 11.5% accuracy on natural-language translation compared to a 28.6% Pass@8 rate on proving human-formalized statements.
Tests an automated research pipeline that produced 64 new claims, of which only 6 survived expert review and formal proof verification due to poor automated research taste.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark highlights that low autoformalization accuracy and poor research intuition are the primary factors preventing LLMs from autonomously conducting theoretical computer science research.

papers.title: When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: A new controlled synthetic benchmark reveals that open-weight LLMs rely on heuristic arbitration strategies, preferring specific modalities and recency over reliability cues when text, numbers, and forecasts conflict.
key_points: benchmark generates latent risk trajectories producing aligned or conflicting numerical time series and natural language summaries.
Experimental framework systematically isolates and manipulates evidence modality, temporal recency, source reliability, and provenance.
Tested open-weight instruction-tuned models exhibit systematic text-versus-number biases and prioritize temporal recency over explicit reliability indicators.
Models demonstrate over-reliance on external tool forecasts, favoring them even when they directly contradict available contextual evidence.
summary.why_it_matters: The heuristic evidence arbitration in current LLMs exposes a critical reliability failure mode for tool-augmented decision-making systems operating on heterogeneous data.

papers.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?

summary.tldr: SWE-bench Science is a repository-level benchmark of 119 tasks across 98 GitHub repositories in 20 domains designed to evaluate coding agents on scientific software engineering.
key_points: Tasks are categorized into three distinct paradigms: Issue-driven, Expert-exploratory, and Engineering-integration.
The top-performing agent, Claude Code with Opus-5 (max), achieved a pass@1 score below 50%.
Agent failures stem from four recurring mechanisms: scientific knowledge deficits, misguided surface-level repairs, incomplete integration, and failure to generalize scientific concepts.

A paired ablation removing explicit scientific guidance revealed that well-grounded scientific information improves performance and token efficiency, whereas poorly aligned guidance causes anchoring without improving repair success.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a concrete framework for identifying how coding agents fail in scientific contexts, where software errors can directly compromise scientific evidence and conclusions.

papers.title: PersonalBench: Measuring the Authorship Gap in LLM Personalization

summary.tldr: PersonalBench evaluates inference-time LLM personalization, revealing that while methods create author-differentiated text, outputs remain dominated by the LLM's own authorship fingerprint and fail to reach human-level stylistic similarity.
key_points: Evaluated 50 authors and 1,000 generations across Qwen 3 and GLM-4 model families using LUAR authorship verification, LLM-as-judge, and stylometrics.
Personalization methods produce author-differentiated text (LUAR AUC=0.918), but all tested methods fall into a narrow LUAR similarity range of 0.484-0.508 to target human authors.
Generated outputs fail to cross the human-LLM boundary, remaining below the cross-author human similarity floor of 0.626 and ceiling of 0.756.
LUAR shows methods are statistically indistinguishable (spread of 0.024), whereas LLM-as-judge discrepancies stem from circularity between trait and profile extraction.
summary.why_it_matters: Current inference-time personalization techniques only modulate LLM style superficially rather than bridging the underlying gap to true human authorship.

infra.title: Exploring Speculative Decoding in vLLM on AMD GPUs

summary.tldr: vLLM supports speculative decoding on AMD Instinct MI300X and MI355X GPUs using ROCm to verify multiple drafted tokens in a single target-model pass.
key_points: Evaluates five speculative drafting approaches: native MTP, Gemma 4 MTP, EAGLE-3, DFlash, and DSpark.
Drafting methods differ by token generation mechanics, including parallel, sequential, autoregressive, and hybrid approaches.
Tested across diverse target models including google/gemma-4-31B-it, Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5.
Throughput gains vary based on proposal length, acceptance behavior, draft checkpoints, and specific workload parameters.
summary.why_it_matters: Speculative decoding allows vLLM users on AMD GPUs to bypass the single-token-per-step latency bottleneck of standard autoregressive decoding while maintaining the target model's output distribution.

summary.tldr: OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT Ads into 31 European markets.
key_points: ChatGPT Ads availability is extending across 31 European markets.
The platform allows advertisers to engage users during exploration, option comparison, and decision-making phases.
summary.why_it_matters: Advertisers in 31 European countries can now target users within ChatGPT during active decision-making workflows.

summary.tldr: Linus Torvalds used an AI model to assist in a difficult debugging session and allowed the AI to write the final Git commit message for the Linux kernel patch drm/xe.
key_points: The AI performed grunt-work during a difficult Linux kernel debugging session, including adding debug code and analyzing the output.
The AI repeatedly claimed the issue was unsolvable and suggested writing a report instead of resolving it, but continued troubleshooting when prompted.
The resulting Linux kernel commit is titled "drm/xe: Don't hand out the flat CCS storage as usable VRAM" and features an AI-written commit message.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that AI can assist with complex low-level Linux kernel debugging when guided by a human developer, despite the model's tendency to give up on hard problems.

summary.tldr: LLM 0.33 upgrades to OpenAI Python library 3.x and httpx2, adds per-call API keys for embeddings, supports chaining prompt templates, and introduces reasoning_summary options.
key_points: Upgraded the OpenAI Python library dependency to version 3.x and switched the underlying HTTP client from httpx to httpx2.

Added --key CLI support to llm embed and llm embed-multi, alongside a key= argument for Python methods (EmbeddingModel.embed(), EmbeddingModel.embed_multi(), Collection.embed(), and Collection.embed_multi()) to pass resolved keys without altering shared model state.
Enabled repeating the -t/--template option in llm prompt to execute multiple templates in order, allowing users to combine model options from one template with prompts from another.
Added support for the reasoning_summary option with auto, concise, and detailed settings for reasoning-capable Responses API models via llm openai endpoint --responses.
summary.why_it_matters: This update aligns embedding key handling with standard LLM models, updates core HTTP dependencies, and enables modular, composable CLI workflows through template chaining.

summary.tldr: Productively using coding agents requires instructing them clearly and verifying changes through methods beyond just line-by-line code review.
key_points: The core skill for using coding agents is confidently instructing changes and verifying their correct execution.
Eyeballing every line of code generated by an agent is not the most effective method for validating software changes.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers must adopt verification strategies beyond manual line-by-line code review to effectively validate AI-generated software changes.

vendors.title: A shot-scraper-style JSON API on Bun 1.4's new Bun.WebView

summary.tldr: Bun 1.4 released with a Rust rewrite and new features including `Bun.WebView`, enabling native browser automation via macOS WebKit or Chromium CDP.
key_points: Bun 1.4 replaces its previous Zig codebase with a Rust rewrite, fixing over 2,900 issues and adding 1,517 Node.js compatibility tests.
Performance improvements in Bun 1.4 include 5x reduced idle CPU usage, up to 35% reduced memory usage, and 50% faster startup on Linux.
New APIs in the release include `Bun.Image`, `Bun.WebView`, `Bun.markdown`, `Bun.cron()`, and `Bun.Terminal`.
A prototype TypeScript web API using `Bun.WebView` required a 192MB-256MB cgroups container to run full Chrome automation against complex web pages.
summary.why_it_matters: `Bun.WebView` provides lightweight, first-class browser automation directly within the runtime without relying on external heavy frameworks.

summary.tldr: OpenAI has joined the PORTS-Pike project to expand community investment and support thousands of jobs in Southern Ohio.
key_points: OpenAI joined the PORTS-Pike project initiative.
The partnership aims to expand community investment in the region.
The initiative supports thousands of jobs located in Southern Ohio.
summary.why_it_matters: The collaboration brings OpenAI's resources to Southern Ohio to support local economic growth and regional job creation.
